title: Health Metrics Dashboard
description: Add system-level health metrics (memory, GC, I/O, WAL, runtime, cycle timing) to the stats pipeline with time-series storage, multi-panel PNG charts, API endpoints, and CLI plotting. Motivated by production OOM kill (Feb 19, exit_code=137). See openspec/changes/health-metrics-dashboard/ for full proposal, design, and specs.

title: Schema migration: add 13 health columns to stats_snapshots
description: Add 13 ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN statements to migrate() in internal/store/store.go. Columns: heap_inuse_bytes, heap_sys_bytes, sys_bytes (INTEGER DEFAULT 0), gc_pause_total_ns, gc_count (INTEGER DEFAULT 0), gc_cpu_fraction (REAL DEFAULT 0), slow_flush_count, slow_flush_max_ms, write_channel_depth, wal_size_bytes, goroutine_count, cycle_duration_ms, trending_duration_ms (INTEGER DEFAULT 0). Follow existing pattern (dropped_posts at line 410) — silently skip duplicate column errors.
acceptance_criteria: All 13 columns exist on stats_snapshots after migrate() runs. Re-running migrate() is idempotent. Partial migration recovery works.

title: Add HEALTH_CHART_HOURS and HEALTH_CHART_MEMORY_LIMIT_MB env vars
description: Add HEALTH_CHART_HOURS (int, default 24, min 1, max 48) and HEALTH_CHART_MEMORY_LIMIT_MB (int, default 1024, 0=disabled) to config parsing in cmd/hourstats/main.go or internal/config/. Clamp out-of-range values and log warning. Invalid non-integer values fall back to defaults with warning. Pass to statsapi server and health chart generator.
acceptance_criteria: HEALTH_CHART_HOURS defaults to 24. Out-of-range clamped to 48 with warning. Non-integer falls back to 24 with warning. HEALTH_CHART_MEMORY_LIMIT_MB defaults to 1024. Set to 0 disables reference line.

title: Implement multi-panel health chart generator
description: Create internal/sparkline/health_chart_generator.go with GenerateHealthChart(snapshots []StatsSnapshot, config HealthChartConfig) ([]byte, error). Render 1200x1600 PNG with 4 stacked panels (each 1200x350, 50px gaps): (1) Memory+GC — HeapInuse/Sys area fill left axis, GCCPUFraction line right axis, optional memory limit dashed line. (2) I/O Pressure — slow_flush_count bars left, write_channel_depth line right. (3) Firehose Volume — total_firehose_posts line, dropped_posts red bars. (4) WAL+Timing — wal_size_bytes area left, cycle_duration_ms line right. Reuse Okabe-Ito palette from DefaultConfig(), axis helpers from axis.go, day/hour marker patterns. Define HealthChartConfig struct and DefaultHealthChartConfig().
acceptance_criteria: GenerateHealthChart returns valid PNG. 4 panels visible with labelled axes. Memory limit line drawn when configured. Handles pre-deployment zero-value snapshots. Fewer than 2 snapshots produces 'Not enough data' image.

title: Add /stats/health/chart API endpoint
description: Add GET /stats/health/chart endpoint to internal/statsapi/server.go. Accept 'hours' query param (int, default from HEALTH_CHART_HOURS env var, min 1, max 48). Fetch health history via GetHealthHistory, pass to GenerateHealthChart with HealthChartConfig (memory limit from HEALTH_CHART_MEMORY_LIMIT_MB). Return PNG with Content-Type image/png. Return 400 for invalid hours param. Return 500 with JSON error if generation fails. Fewer than 2 snapshots returns a 'not enough data' PNG.
acceptance_criteria: Endpoint returns PNG image. Default hours from env var. Custom hours param works. Invalid param returns 400. Generation error returns 500 JSON. Content-Type is image/png.

title: Add CLI plot command with ASCII sparklines
description: Add 'plot' subcommand to cmd/hourstats-stats/main.go. Accept --hours flag (int, default 24) and --endpoint flag (string, default from env or http://localhost:9111). Fetch from /stats/health/history API. Render 8 ASCII sparkline rows using Unicode braille characters (60 chars wide): HeapInuse (MB), GC CPU Fraction (%), WAL Size (MB), Channel Depth, Slow Flushes, Cycle Duration (s), Firehose Posts, Dropped Posts. Each row: metric name (20 chars left-aligned), sparkline, min/max/current. Exit 1 if API unreachable. Exit 0 with message if no data.
acceptance_criteria: plot command renders 8 sparkline rows. Custom --hours works. API error prints to stderr, exits 1. Empty data prints message, exits 0. No new dependencies.

title: Extend StatsSnapshot struct and INSERT/SELECT queries
description: Add 13 new fields to StatsSnapshot struct in internal/store/stats.go with json tags matching column names. Update InsertStatsSnapshot() to include all new fields in the INSERT statement. Update GetLatestSnapshot() and GetSnapshotHistory() SELECT statements to read all new columns. Pre-migration rows will return 0 for new fields (DEFAULT 0).
acceptance_criteria: StatsSnapshot struct has all 13 new fields. InsertStatsSnapshot writes them. GetLatestSnapshot and GetSnapshotHistory read them. Round-trip insert/read preserves all values.

title: Add memory and GC metrics to stats collector
description: Add SampleSystemMetrics() method to internal/stats/collector.go that calls runtime.ReadMemStats() and stores HeapInuse, HeapSys, Sys, GCCPUFraction. Add atomic fields for previous PauseTotalNs and NumGC to compute per-interval deltas. On first snapshot after startup, deltas are 0. Call SampleSystemMetrics() from TakeSnapshot(). Also read runtime.NumGoroutine() and store as goroutine_count.
acceptance_criteria: TakeSnapshot() populates heap_inuse_bytes, heap_sys_bytes, sys_bytes, gc_pause_total_ns (delta), gc_count (delta), gc_cpu_fraction, and goroutine_count. First snapshot has 0 for GC deltas.

title: Add slow flush counter and channel depth to stats collector
description: Add IncrementSlowFlush(durationMs int64) method to collector that atomically increments slow flush count and updates max if new value is larger. Add SampleWriteChannelDepth(depth int) method. In TakeSnapshot(), read and reset slow flush count/max (atomic swap to 0), read channel depth. Store as slow_flush_count, slow_flush_max_ms, write_channel_depth on the snapshot.
acceptance_criteria: IncrementSlowFlush accumulates count and tracks max. Counters reset to 0 after each TakeSnapshot. write_channel_depth reflects point-in-time len(writeCh).

title: Wire writer goroutine to report slow flushes to collector
description: In cmd/hourstats/writer.go, after detecting a slow flush (>1s threshold, already logged), call collector.IncrementSlowFlush(durationMs). The writer goroutine needs a reference to the stats collector, passed during initialization in main.go. Also wire SampleWriteChannelDepth: pass len(writeCh) to the collector at TakeSnapshot time from main.go.
acceptance_criteria: Writer goroutine calls IncrementSlowFlush on each slow flush. TakeSnapshot receives current write channel depth. No new goroutines or channels added.

title: Add WAL file size sampling to stats collector
description: Add WAL file size reading to TakeSnapshot(). Use os.Stat(dbPath + "-wal") where dbPath is provided at collector initialization. If file not found, store 0. If other os.Stat error, log warning and store 0. Store as wal_size_bytes on the snapshot.
acceptance_criteria: wal_size_bytes reflects actual WAL file size. Missing WAL file returns 0. Permission errors log warning and return 0.

title: Add cycle duration tracking to analysis pipeline
description: Add RecordCycleDuration(totalMs int64) and RecordTrendingDuration(trendingMs int64) methods to collector. These store values as simple int64 fields (single-writer, read at snapshot time). In cmd/hourstats/analysis.go, call RecordCycleDuration before returning from runAnalysisCycle(). In the trending analysis function, call RecordTrendingDuration. TakeSnapshot reads and stores as cycle_duration_ms/trending_duration_ms, then resets to 0.
acceptance_criteria: cycle_duration_ms and trending_duration_ms are populated after analysis cycles. Values are 0 when no cycle ran in the interval. Trending disabled produces trending_duration_ms=0.

title: Add GetHealthHistory store method and StatsStore interface extension
description: Add GetHealthHistory(ctx context.Context, since time.Time, limit int) ([]StatsSnapshot, error) to internal/store/stats.go. Query stats_snapshots for ALL columns (existing + 13 new) where snapshot_time >= since, ORDER BY snapshot_time ASC, LIMIT. Add the method to the StatsStore interface in internal/statsapi/server.go. This method is used by both /stats/health/history and /stats/health/chart endpoints.
acceptance_criteria: GetHealthHistory returns chronologically ordered snapshots with all health fields. Respects time filter and limit. Added to StatsStore interface.

title: Add /stats/health/history API endpoint
description: Add GET /stats/health/history endpoint to internal/statsapi/server.go. Accept 'hours' query param (int, default 24, min 1, max 48 — clamp if out of range). Return JSON array of health-relevant fields from StatsSnapshot, ordered oldest-first. Return HTTP 200 with application/json. Empty array if no data.
acceptance_criteria: Endpoint returns JSON array of health snapshots. Default 24h window. Custom hours param works. Out-of-range clamped to 48. Empty window returns []. Content-Type is application/json.

title: Improve Gemini topic labeling with current-event context
description: Gemini mislabels topics when it lacks current-event awareness. Examples: 'IIHF World Championship' for what was actually the Olympic hockey gold medal game; 'Greenland ice sheet' for US-Greenland political relations. The LLM groups the right keywords but picks wrong event names because it has no real-time context. Potential approaches: (1) feed trending news headlines into the prompt as context, (2) include post text samples alongside TF-IDF terms so Gemini can infer the actual event, (3) use a news API to provide current-event grounding, (4) add a post-hoc label correction step using exemplar post content.
